timed_text.text: day 28, who are you in a guitar? Not who you are in your best day, not who you want to be,
who are you when you're behind in the fourth quarter, when you've made two mistakes back to back,
when the biggest competition of your season is on the line and everything in your body is asking
you to quit. Think back to where you were when this journey started. There was probably a
version of you that didn't have an answer for that question. That defaulted to the situation,
that got swallowed by the moment. You've been building the answer for 28 days.
The mental training doesn't change you in the comfortable moments. It reveals you in the difficult
ones. Every rep you've put in has been preparing you for exactly that moment, the one that
used to break you. Today I want you to write your competition identity, not a general statement.
The version of you that shows up when the game is on the line and everything is against you.
On your screen, we're going to take a breath and then we write.

cards.prompt: Write your competition identity statement — specifically for your hardest moment. Who are you when the game is on the line, you're behind, and everything hurts? Present tense. 'I am an athlete who...'

timed_text.text: Read that before every competition from here forward.
Not as a wish as a reminder of a decision you've already made.
You have a journal prompt and after you finish day 28 is complete.

blocks.prompt: When was the last time you actually lived out that identity in competition? What made it possible?
